This disasterous division led to the historical Tahkim (judgment between 'Ali and Mu'awiyah to determine who is worthy of Khilafah), and to bitter wars between the two feuding factions. The Tahkim itself resulted in more division within the ummah: four different groups were formed:

1. The majority of Muslims remained solidly behind the caliph 'Ali, since he was the legitimate, shura-selected Amir-ul-Mu'minin (the caliph selected by general consensus of the leaders and representatives of all Muslims), following the assassination of the third caliph 'Uthman.

2. The party of Mu'awiyah which was initially formulated to "avenge the death of 'Uthman," but ended up demanding the caliphate for their leader Mu'awiyah. Following the Tahkim, this group did capture the caliphate, and Mu'awiyah became the ruler of the torn ummah.

3. The Khawarij (The Rebels) who were supporters of 'Ali, but rebelled against him for accepting the Tahkim; they declared that only Allah had the power of Tahkim. At the same time, they violently opposed Mu'awiyah for wanting to snatch the caliphate away from 'Ali.

4. Following the martyrdom of Amir-ul-Mu'minin 'Ali, some of his supporters formed the Shi'ah party and demanded restoration of caliphate to Ahlul Bait ('Ali's family).

The Falsification

Since each one of the above mentioned parties wanted to muster the allegiance of the Muslim ummah, they sought to support their political views by Qur'anic statements and sunnah traditions. Thus, some of them resorted to flagrant misinterpretations of the Qur'an; some even attempted to falsify the Qur'an itself. With the divine guarantee of the Qur'an's integrity, those who attempted to distort the Qur'an were immediately exposed. Too many people had already committed the Qur'an to their memory, and the Qur'an distorters got nowhere. What they succeeded in, however, was the injection of false Hadiths into the Prophet's traditions, as well as misinterpreting the existing Hadiths. With the passage of time, so many false Hadiths were fabricated that the authentic Hadiths became almost completely indistinguishable from the false ones. The first falsified Hadiths were characterized by the praise and over-glorification of certain individuals, such as the four great caliphs, and Ahlul Bait; something they neither needed nor advocated. Then, other fabrications of Hadiths dealt with the establishment of certain political parties and various religious sects. With the appearance of each political group, a number of fabricated Hadiths showed up supporting the creation of such

The Prophet's companions (peace be upon them) were not as susceptible to deceit by false Hadiths as those of later generations. With the emergence of these groups, the falsification of Hadith intensified; each group seeking to support its own views, and its own leaders. The time when falsification started, therefore, should be tied with the appearance of these and other political parties. Iraq became so famous for fabricating Hadith that it became known as "The Mint;" Hadith was coined there like Dirhams. In Medina, meanwhile, Imam Malik advised the Muslims, "Look on the Hadith of the Iraqis the way you look on the Hadith of the people of the scripture (Jews and Christian); neither believe, nor disbelieve them." 'Abdul-Rahman b. Mahdi once told Malik, "During my 40-day visit to Medina, I learned only 400 Hadiths; Back home in Iraq, we hear this same number of Hadiths in one day." Imam Malik replied, "In Iraq you have 'The Mint;' you coin Hadith during the night, and spend during the day." Another reflection on the Iraqi fabrication of Hadith is recorded in the remark by Ibn Shihab that "The Hadith which leaves Medina only on Shibr (10 inches) long, comes back from Iraq one Dhira' (one yard) long."

2. Influence of the Enemies of Islam:
When Islam brought down the two great empires, Rome and Persia, the people of those empires were freed from exploitation and downright slavery to their rulers. The rulers, their supporters, and the oppressing class in general, sought to discredit Islam in the minds of their people who were adopting the freedom-giving Islam in great numbers. Thus, they fabricated repulsive Hadiths aiming at preventing their people from converting to Islam. Examples of their fabrications include a Hadith which states, "A group of Jews debated with the Prophet and asked him, 'Who carries the throne of Allah,' and he answered, 'The throne is carried on the horns of insects,' Whereupon, the Jews said, 'We bear witness that you are indeed the messenger of Allah.'" This and similar Hadiths were easily detectable due to their naivity [naivety]; all Muslims would realize right away that such statements with their contradictions could not have come from the Prophet. Another example is the fabricated Hadith, "The Prophet was asked, 'What is God made from?' He answered, 'He is made from running liquid; He created horses, made them run until they perspired heavily, then He created Himself from the sweat.'" Certainly, no Muslim, nor a person in his complete mind would fabricate a Hadith like that. These enemies of Islam inflicted great harm through the frequency and abominability of their lies. One of them who had named himself 'Abdul-Karim b. Abul-'Awja' admitted that he fabricated 4,000 Hadiths making things Halal (permissable) and other things Haram (prohibited). A great number of this type of fabricated Hadith (fabricated by enemies of Islam), as high as 14,000, were detected and sifted out by Muslim scholars in the past centuries.

The Muslim non-Arabs felt this discrimination and sought to establish the rule of Islam; based on absolute equality among the races. This racial friction resulted in the fabrication of a number of Hadiths praising and/or downgrading certain races, languages, towns, etc. Examples of such Hadiths include, "Those around the throne of Allah speak Persian; when Allah issues a merciful command, He issues it in Persian; when the command involves punishment, He issues it in Arabic." transcription_text:
THE FALSIFICATION OF HADITH

The above quoted Hadith is recorded by Tabari, Hakim, Nabahani (in his "Arba'een"), Sayuti (in his 'Ehya-ul-Mayyit) and by others.
Here is another Tradition:

[Arabic Hadith text]

"The stars protect the inhabitants of the earth from being drowned and my Ahlul-Bait are the Protectors of my followers against discord (in matters of religion). Therefore, whichever group among the Arabs opposes my Ahlil-Bait (on questions relating to the divine Commandments) shall be split up by dissensions and become the party of Satan."

The above quoted Hadith is recorded by Imam Hakim, in his Mustadrak, vol. 3, p. 149, as related by Ibn-e-Abbas with the note that this is an authentic tradition but has not been recorded by the two Shaikhs, Muslim & Bukhari!!!

ALI IN THE QURAN
There are so many verses in the Holy Quran praising Imam Ali, Alaihis-Salam. There is no room here to quote all or even few of them. "Islamic Affairs" will try her best to show these verses to her readers, both Muslims and non-Muslims in her future issues, Insha-Allah.
When Hazrat Ali stayed in the Prophet's own bed while the infidels wanted to assasinate [assassinate] the Prophet, he became the first person to make sacrifices for Divine Right. Then the verse "And there is the type of man who gives his life to earn the pleasure of God; and God is full of kindness to (His) devotees" (Quran, II:207) was revealed for him.
According to the most authoritative books in Sunnat and Jama'at: one day the Prophet of Islam assembled Ali, Fatimah, Hassan and Hussain (AS) under a robe and the verse, "And God only wishes to remove all abomination from you, ye Members of the Family (Ahlil-Bait), and to make you pure and spotless" (Quran, XXXIII:33) was then revealed on their behalf from the Almighty. This is referred to as "hadees-e-Kisa" (Hadees of the Robe).

THE PROPHET (SA) SAID:
I am the city of learning, Ali is its gate.
Ali is with the Quran and the Quran is with Ali.
Ali is the treasure-house of my secrets.
I am the last of the Apostles of God (Khatamul-Nabiyyeen), O Ali, whilst you are the last of the successors to the Prophets (Khatamul-Wasiyyeen)
Ali is to me what Harron (Aron) was to Moosa (Moses).
O Ali! You are my brother in this world as well as the Hereafter.
I have left amongst you, O ye people, certain things, if you will love them you will never go astray. They are: the Book of Allah (Quran), which is like a rope extending from the heaven to the earth, and my children, that is my Ahl-e-Bait. These two shall never part from each other until they come to me at the Pool of Kausar (in Paradise). So, take care how you treat them.

ALI AS CALIPH (36 A.H.)
In the year 36 Hijri, Hazrat Ali was elected Caliph, succeeding Uthman who was murdered due to his being unfair to the public and his preference of his unfit relatives for government offices. The first thing he did was dismissing all the corrupt governors previously appointed (by the previous Caliphs). Qualities of honesty and justice did not allow him to pay heed even to the advice of his uncle Ibne Abbas. Some gave up the office without resistance, while others revolted.
